On his first day as project lead at a Mumbai software firm, Tarun didn't start with tasks. He started with a date.
The client demo was on 20 September. He wrote it in red on the office whiteboard. Then he counted back. Integration testing needed a fortnight, so it began 6 September. Coding had to finish before that, so 5 September. Design had to be signed off by 10 August to leave enough coding time.
His teammate Mridul watched. "You're planning backwards."
"The demo won't move," Tarun said. "Everything else has to fit behind it."
By lunch he had built a shared calendar with each deadline marked, and sent it to the whole team. In the afternoon meeting he put it on the screen. "This is the one calendar we all look at."
Mridul pointed at 6 September. "So if design slips, testing gets squeezed?"
"Exactly. That's why design has the earliest deadline."

qa.q: What was the date of the client demo?
qa.a: The client demo was on 20 September.

qa.q: What does Tarun's calm answer suggest about how he felt as a new lead?
qa.a: It suggests he felt confident and clear, sure that the fixed demo date should shape everything else.

qa.q: What else could Tarun do to protect the testing window?
qa.a: He could check design progress weekly before 10 August, so any slip is caught before it squeezes testing.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Mridul?
qa.a: Mridul quickly sees the link between design slipping and testing getting squeezed, showing the calendar made the risks clear to the team.

"Chandrika, day one and you're already drawing calendars?" Jagdish laughed, pulling up a chair in the Pune office.
"The client demo is 15 November. That's fixed." She tapped the date on her screen. "So let's work backwards."
"From the end?"
"Integration testing needs two weeks. So it starts 1 November."
"And coding?"
"Finishes 31 October. Which means design is signed off by 30 September."
Jagdish frowned. "That's only three weeks for design."
"Yes. So if design isn't finished by 30 September, we know immediately we're in trouble, not in November."
"Okay," he said slowly. "Who sees this?"
"Everyone. Today." She shared the calendar to the team channel. "One calendar, all deadlines. No surprises."
Jagdish scrolled through it. "It's scary seeing it all at once."
"Better scary now than in November."
